body: May be '.No' is correct column name too? In this case, we need to add check if dot is first or last.

`No.` is not a valid PHP property name so there is no point in supporting such column names on the AR level. Also allowing `.` in normal column names would complicate the code for automatic quoting of column names and may even make it impossible.

issue.title: Query builder incorrectly quotes column alias in select

repository.name: yii2
repository.description: Yii 2: The Fast, Secure and Professional PHP Framework

issue.body:
The code:

```
$rows = (new \yii\db\Query())->select(['a.b' => new \yii\db\Expression('123')])->all();
```

produces incorrect SQL:

```
SELECT 123 AS `a`.`b`
```

The SQL should be:

```
SELECT 123 AS `a.b`
```

body: **cebe** But its valid column name and you can access it by $model->{'No.'}

>  No.  is not a valid PHP property name

"No." is completely standard SQL compliant identifier when properly quoted. 

> so there is no point in supporting such column names on the AR level.

There is a point when the result of AR is converted into array (with `toArray()`) and the alias becomes a key in the array - no problems using array key with a dot in PHP whatsoever.

Currently there is no workaround at all (other than not using Query Builder) to produce an SQL with an alias having a dot - neither manual alias quoting using {{ }} symbols, nor using `\yii\db\Expression` helps. This must be supported on the framework level.

> This must be supported on the framework level.

I fully support this. It have to be done.

Another case,  '[No.]' is valid name too.
In case of:

> $man = Model::find()->andFilterWhere(['like', '[No.]', '62821'])->count();

will break query too.

Problem is in the **vendor/yiisoft/yii2/db/Schema.php:523**
I think, there have to be:

> if (strpos($name, '(') !== false || strpos($name, '[[') !== false || strpos($name, '{{') !== false **|| (substr($name, 0, 1) === '[' && substr($name, -1, 1) === ']')**) {..}

Instead of:

> if (strpos($name, '(') !== false || strpos($name, '[[') !== false || strpos($name, '{{') !== false) {

But all of this are a crutch :) We need more more general solution for this.
